answer: The bond is keyed to a hardware root, so one machine backs one identity unless you buy another chip. If the audit panel for an epoch lacks diversity, the stake is voided and the identity refunds nothing. Auditors rotate in from a pool with no warning, so a farm cannot know who grades it before the quartz is committed. In practice one chip backs one identity and the panel rotates anyway. A marble of extra keys does not help when the ember of one burned bond costs more than the payout.
